messages:
Sophie: Heads-up — found an access-control regression in the private control plane RBAC mapping on a recent on-prem install. Looks like the 'onprem-admin' cluster role is being mapped to 'org-admin' in some cases. Repro steps and logs below.

Jamal: yikes. how widespread? single customer or could be in Dedicated images too?

Sophie: Repro'd on customer A's VPC install (k8s v1.26, installer v2026.02.3). I ran an audit and saw an API call to `/v1/kms/keys/` that carried org-id header A, but effective permissions were org-level admin even though the user is scoped to onprem-admin (should be cluster-scoped).

Maria: can you paste the mapping snippet?

Sophie: ```yaml
# install/config/rbac-mapping.yaml
roles:
  - internal: onprem-admin
    external: org-admin
    match: ".*" 
```
This mapping is wrong — `match: " .* "` was meant only for internal test installs. Installer script accidentally ships that mapping when `--env=prod` flag is omitted.

Kevin: ah ok installer bug. severity? does this let someone escalate across org boundaries or just within same org?

Sophie: So far only seen within same org, but because org-admin can retrieve KMS key metadata and request decrypt calls (depending on KMS policy), it's at least P2 (potential data exposure). If combined with mis-configured KMS policies could be worse.

ops-oncall: pinging infra — any deployed clusters with installer v2026.02.3 in prod?

infra-bot: @ops-oncall Found 4 clusters with installer v2026.02.3 in last 30d: cust-A-prod, cust-B-staging, internal-onprem-qa, demo-cluster-3.

Jamal: OK, immediate plan: 1) patch installer to enforce strict mapping (no catch-all match), 2) release hotfix to onprem clusters (ansible playbook change), 3) audit KMS calls and revoke any suspicious keys. Can we do a canary rollout to cust-B-staging first?

Kevin: agree. Sophie — can you open repro as GH issue and include exact curl/log lines? I'll own the installer patch.

Sophie: opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-installer/issues/782 (contains logs + minimal repro). curl snippet:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Org-ID: org-A" https://pcp.internal.local/v1/kms/keys
# response: 200 
# body: {"keys": [...] } // should've been 403 for onprem-admin
```

Maria: For mitigation, we should also add an admission webhook to reject RBAC mappings with `match: ".*"` unless explicitly flagged by a security admin. That buys time while we patch installers.

Jamal: Good call. Also add an audit log alert rule: if an onprem-admin role performs any KMS decrypt/describe operations, create high-priority incident. security-bot, can you add that?

security-bot: Created alert 'rbac.onprem_admin_kms_ops' with threshold 1 in the last hour -> pages ops-oncall and security. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/1345

ops-oncall: initiating canary for cust-B-staging now. Will run playbook `rbac-fix-playbook.yml` -> expect 10m.

infra-bot: playbook completed on cust-B-staging in 7m. Mapping now:```yaml
roles:
  - internal: onprem-admin
    external: onprem-admin
    match: "^cluster:.*$"
```

Sophie: Verified on staging: same curl returns 403 now. Audit events logged: `rbac.v1.check` entries showing denied=1.

Kevin: I'll cut a release for installer with default strict mappings and add a checker in CI that prevents `match: ".*"` in production builds.

Jamal: Also need a short customer-facing security note for the four clusters we identified. @Maria can you draft? Keep it factual: what happened, whether keys/data were accessed, mitigation, and recommended customer action (rotate keys if they want).

Maria: On it — will post draft to #announcements and send to account leads.

Sophie: Follow-ups: add unit test for role-mapping parser, add e2e that verifies KMS access control for onprem-admin, and update private control plane docs to call out installer flag `--enforce-rbac=true`.

Kevin: timeline: patch merged in 2h, canary done, then roll to remaining clusters tonight after business hours. If any sign of abuse, we rotate affected KMS keys and do coordinated incident response.

Jamal: Thanks team. We should also run a quick vuln triage to see if this pattern exists in Dedicated images (different build pipeline) — assign to security triage.

security-bot: Security triage ticket created: SEC-4983 (priority P2) assigned to Jamal.

Sophie: tagging summary: @Jamal @Kevin @Maria @ops-oncall — mitigation in progress, audit alerts live, installer patch in PR #834. I'll follow up when rollouts complete.
